Aggregating repeated orientations and removing equal opposite weights preserves balance and leaves paired contribution equal to one half times its removed weight, because the section is volume-null in the simplex.

For each vertex label the uncanceled weight is signed according to orientation. Multiplying by f_i converts the balance equation to the one-dimensional raw-gradient relation spanned by t_i, so all nonzero signed weights have the same sign. Normalizing the remainder gives exactly the predecessor's θ_i or its reversal. Labels with t_i=0 contribute only through canceled pairs.

Checked the duplicate-label triangle λ=(1/2,1/3,1/6) exactly. Its two coincident sections have opposite oriented normalized vectors with equal norm, and their cap fractions are 1/3 and 2/3. Any assignment to a legal label yields the same physical balance, so the signed-kernel argument continues to apply.

When all coordinates satisfy the cutoff, t is a probability vector of length m=d+1. Uniform t is equivalent to uniform λ, and the reversed mean is at least one half. When one coordinate exceeds the cutoff only its own label is available; either orientation has the same positive section area, so balance forces half weight on each. When two exceed, none is available. In d=1 section area is one, including at an endpoint, and the two intervals have complementary lengths.
